extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and stakeholders (advertisers, publishers, policymakers) during wartime
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and description of how newspapers, advertising, circulation and rationing policy operate under wartime conditions, including government advertising priority, paper/economy measures, and tire/gasoline rationing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of newspaper space devoted to advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising now fills about 23 per cent of the total space in the newspapers (compared with about 42 per cent before the war).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Of this available space, the government buys a large proportion. There is a nominal figure of 25 per cent of the available space which the government may take, but it can, of course, always get more if it wishes, according to the importance of the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government priority for advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority is not given to any advertiser except the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The government's advertising invariably is designed to stimulate war savings drives, fuel-conservation campaigns, ATS recruiting efforts and similar war work. The government pays the regular space rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift toward institutional/prestige advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Wartime conditions favor institutional and good-will or prestige advertising rather than product advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Much space is bought simply to keep business or industrial names before the public; otherwise new competitors coming in after the war would have an equal or even better merchandising chance. Some firms buy space for prestige even when supplies (e.g., whisky) are relatively meager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction and repricing of classified advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Classified advertising columns and availability have been drastically reduced compared with pre-war levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Daily Telegraph carried an average of 50 columns of classified daily before the war; today it has only eight columns in a six-page paper and four and a quarter columns in a four-page paper. A representative afternoon paper has less than a column of classified advertising sold at $2.50 a line compared with rates of 60 to 85 cents a line three years ago. Papers state they could take more copy if they had the available space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper production economies under wartime shortages
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspapers adopt measures to economize print resources to maintain circulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques include using thinner paper to provide more copies, designing make-up to get more words into smaller spaces, using larger type faces, wide margins, and other layout adjustments to conserve newsprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on street and outlet sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Street sales of newspapers are limited and of brief duration; supplies allotted to news agents in railroad stations, subways and hotels are exhausted quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residents of small towns, villages and rural areas often find it extremely difficult to get any papers except occasional copies; subscription and distribution constraints are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing capacity limits on increasing circulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspaper executives state they could increase sales substantially if additional printing means/materials were available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: a London afternoon paper could sell between 200,000 and 300,000 extra papers daily if there were means of printing them; the Daily Express could add at least 200,000 subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic tire inspections as a requirement for ration renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodic tire inspections will be required as part of registration/renewal for tire/gasoline rationing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of Price Administration (OPA) said it would announce details of the periodic tire-inspection program shortly. Registration begins November 9; inspections will be a requirement for renewal of rations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification limit of five tires per vehicle
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must certify they own no more than five tires for any vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant lists more than five tires for each car, he will be denied an 'A' book until he shows he has disposed of the excess tires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing serial numbers of all tires on registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant will be required to list the serial numbers of all tires he owns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This listing is part of the registration process beginning November 9; it enables enforcement of the five-tire certification and allocation of coupons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation or reduction of rations for speeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Rations may be revoked or reduced for drivers who exceed the 35-mile-an-hour speed limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to reduce overall mileage and conserve rubber by discouraging high-speed driving which increases tire wear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental ration qualification criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for a supplemental (additional) ration, an applicant must show occupational need beyond the basic allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must show he needs more than 150 miles per month of occupational driving and, if applicable, demonstrate participation in a car-sharing club (car pool) for carrying three or more persons to and from work regularly. Applications for supplemental rations may be filed any time after the basic ('A') book has been received.

rubrics_metrics.name: National mileage reduction targets
rubrics_metrics.description: The rationing plan is geared to reduce the national average mileage to a specified target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan was described as designed to reduce the national average mileage to 5,000 a year (with other references to a rate of 2,880 per year appearing for allocation details). The program ties tire/coupon allocation to these mileage targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for centralization of procurement and ration administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Labor delegates recommended centralizing responsibilities for procurement, wages authority and rationing administration under national-level bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific recommendations included centralizing responsibility for all procurement in the chairman of the War Production Board, granting full authority over wages to the War Labor Board, and administering all rationing by the Director of Economic Stabilization. The rationale: centralization aids planning, efficient use of civilian sacrifices, and coherent overall wartime economic policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFL recommendation to consolidate rationing under Director of Economic Stabilization
rubrics_metrics.description: The American Federation of Labor urged that all rationing in the United States be placed under the Director of Economic Stabilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AFL's executive council criticized the Office of Price Administration for piecemeal administration and recommended consolidation to ensure consistent policy and administration. The report noted insufficient representative local boards (about 1,600 labor representatives on 5,000 rationing boards) and recommended improved administration.
